prompt: State the three rules that generate the happens-before relation.
accepted: local order send before receive transitivity
same process send receive transitive closure
solution: Use local event order, send-before-receive, and transitivity.
explanation: These rules define the causal relation without requiring a global clock.
misconception: Local order alone is incomplete; message edges and transitive closure are also generators of happens-before.
visualHook: Draw one local edge, one send-to-receive edge, and a transitive path in different styles.

prompt: Why is concurrency not the same as simultaneous wall-clock time?
accepted: concurrency means neither happens before the other
wall clock is not causal order
solution: Concurrency is defined by incomparability under happens-before; two events can be concurrent even if their physical timestamps differ.
explanation: A timestamp ordering is not automatically a causal proof.
misconception: Different wall-clock values do not establish causality when no allowed event or message path connects them.
visualHook: Compare two vertically aligned events on separate timelines with no message edge.
